title: 125. Divine Mercy - Solemnity of All Saints!

reels.title: Jesus Did Not Have a Microphone and That Is Why He Had to Speak from the Heart
reels.hook: Why did Jesus have to shout?
reels.why: An unexpected and witty comparison with a concrete image: Jesus on the mount without a microphone and a speaker at promotions with a microphone. The thought is rounded off with a clear insight about speaking from the heart and is understandable without the rest of the show.
reels.speaker: Vladimir Grebenar
speakers: Vladimir Grebenar (according to metadata; does not introduce himself by name in the transcript)
reels.quote: Because without a microphone when you speak you have to speak from the heart.

cards.text: Why did Jesus have to shout?
Vladimir Grebenar · host, Ora et Labora
Commentary on the Gospel of the Beatitudes on the Solemnity of All Saints
“Because without a microphone when you speak you have to speak from the heart.”

reels.title: “I Did Not Take One Cent for Myself”: Response to Accusations About Donations
reels.hook: Accused of taking money from donations. Here is the answer
reels.why: A direct and emotional response to a concrete accusation, with clear details: private car, own fuel and accommodation. The controversy holds attention, and the thought is rounded off.

reels.title: Vision in Prayer: An Angel Releases Something from His Hand, and Europe Is Burning
reels.hook: In prayer he saw an angel releasing something from his hand
reels.why: A personal testimony about a vision in prayer is connected with concrete countries and events (Germany, Italy, unrest). The image and claim immediately create tension.
reels.speaker: Vladimir Grebenar
speakers: Vladimir Grebenar (according to metadata; does not introduce himself by name in the transcript)
reels.quote: What I saw in prayer some few months ago that the number of cities will increase, that riots, unrest will erupt.

reels.title: All Saints Is Not a Day for the Cemetery, but a Family Slava
reels.hook: On All Saints you go to the cemetery? Wrong day
reels.why: It breaks a widespread habit (cemetery on All Saints) and gives a practical suggestion: family lunch and celebration, comparable to the Orthodox slava. It ends with a memorable point.
reels.speaker: Vladimir Grebenar
speakers: Vladimir Grebenar (according to metadata; does not introduce himself by name in the transcript)
reels.quote: God glorified the saints because they glorified him.

reels.title: The Devil Cannot Do Anything Until God Permits Him
reels.why: A short, clear theological assertion with a biblical example (Jesus and Peter, sifting wheat). It offers a consoling point: temptation serves the purification of the Church.
reels.speaker: Vladimir Grebenar
speakers: Vladimir Grebenar (according to metadata; does not introduce himself by name in the transcript)
reels.quote: The devil cannot take mastery over the world for a certain time until God the Father permits him that.

reels.title: Call to Croats for God's Uprising: Fasting, Prayer, Penance
reels.hook: Croats need an uprising, but God's
reels.why: A strong and provocative call with clear content. The contrast of the weak spirituality of the West and hope for the Croatian people gives it emotion and direction.
reels.speaker: Vladimir Grebenar
speakers: Vladimir Grebenar (according to metadata; does not introduce himself by name in the transcript)
reels.quote: That is why the Croatian people must rise up in an uprising, but God's battle, God's uprising, fasting, prayer, penance.

reels.title: If You Rejoice in the Gospel, You Have Already Stepped into Eternity
reels.hook: What has God prepared for us? Nobody knows
reels.why: A personal, joyful emotion before an uncertain eternity and a simple sign for the viewer how to recognize that they are on the right path.
reels.speaker: Vladimir Grebenar
speakers: Vladimir Grebenar (according to metadata; does not introduce himself by name in the transcript)
reels.quote: And if you can rejoice in God's word, the Gospel, that means you are on the right path because you have already now stepped into eternity.
